Subject: Edgebridge demarcation & egress guard — initial topology and questions

Hi Naomi / team,

Thanks again for taking a look. Attached is our current site topology (brightline-topology-v1.drawio.png) and a short matrix of requirements (network-requirements.xlsx). We're planning a private deployment of Redwood in our colo (site-a) and a DR presence in the cloud region (us-east-2). High-level asks:

- Validate the demarcation between our edge bridge (L3 fabric) and Redwood's runtime: we want the data-plane to remain wholly in our network, with the control path able to reach Redwood's control plane over a managed tunnel.
- Recommend an egress-guard pattern for model telemetry and metrics so we can retain observability without exposing tenant data.
- Failover: an expected behavior if site-a loses WAN connectivity — can requests be routed to the cloud region gracefully, and what state (KV cache) will be lost vs. persisted?
- MTU/BFD: any constraints we should plan for with jumbo frames and BFD timers for BGP?

Can we schedule an architecture readout + walkthrough early next week? We're targeting a preflight cutover three weeks from now and want to lock the topology and runbook.

Attachments: brightline-topology-v1.drawio.png, network-requirements.xlsx

Alex — thanks for the clear pack and runbook target. I reviewed the drawio and requirements and attached an annotated PDF with our recommendations (redwood-annotated-topology-v1.pdf). High-level notes up front:

1) Demarcation model (control vs. data):
   - Data plane: keep entirely inside Brightline's L3 fabric as requested. Runtime nodes (inference) should only accept tenant traffic from your tenant switch via the demarcation router; no public egress on those interfaces.
   - Control plane: we recommend a single outbound TLS tunnel from a small control-plane proxy cluster in your site to our control endpoint. That proxy handles model rollouts, health pings, and function/tool call coordination.

2) Egress guard & telemetry:
   - Two-channel telemetry: (a) model/usage metrics (aggregated, no raw prompts) over the control tunnel; (b) optional secure syslog/metrics export to your SIEM via a mirrored, scrubbed stream.
   - We'll provide a filter profile to redact anything resembling PII before any telemetry leaves the site. That lives as a policy on the proxy cluster and is configurable per-tenant.

3) Failover behavior and KV cache:
   - Short answer: can failover, but KV cache is local. If we failover to cloud region, warmed caches and decoding state will not be present — cold-start latency expected for sessions that depend on large KV caches. We propose a graceful fallback policy: stable requests go to cloud variant (quantized/compat) and session-level retries surface to the app with a clear 429/503 fallback.

4) MTU & BGP timers:
   - Recommend 1500 MTU unless you plan jumbo frames end-to-end; we have observed occasional packet fragmentation issues across some colo fabrics when mixed MTU is present. BFD: aggressive timers (50ms) can be brittle; suggest 100/300 for detect/hold in the preflight, tighten after cutover testing.

5) Canary criteria and runbook asks (what we'd like from Brightline):
   - A short prompt set for quality regression testing post-quant/opt changes.
   - A traffic shadowing window (2h) with sample qps to warm caches.
   - Contact list for NOC+network on call during cutover.

Next steps: can we do a 45-minute readout Tuesday 2027-08-31 10:00–10:45 PT? If that works I will share a short agenda and a draft runbook checklist.

Attachments: redwood-annotated-topology-v1.pdf

Best,

Redwood Inference

Thanks Naomi and Alex — brief follow-up from infra/ops perspective. Picking up Naomi's notes and converting them into concrete checklist items for the cutover runbook. Inline where helpful: 

> 1) Demarcation model (control vs. data):
- Agree with the outbound-only control proxy. Add: pin TLS termination to the proxy and prefer mTLS between proxies and Redwood control endpoints for mutual auth.

> 2) Egress guard & telemetry:
- We'll provide the redact profile Naomi mentioned. Operational ask for Brightline: confirm whether your SIEM accepts compressed msgpack; if yes, we can use a compressed telemetry stream to reduce bandwidth.

> 3) Failover behavior and KV cache:
- For session-sensitive apps, recommend an optional lightweight replication approach: a per-shard last-known-kv snapshot pushed to object storage with signed access for cloud region warmup. It's not realtime (adds ~20–30s), but reduces cold-start latency for a subset of sessions. This will be opt-in and must be approved from a compliance standpoint.

> 4) MTU & BGP timers:
- We'll mirror Naomi's recommendation. Test matrix: 1500 vs 9000 MTU across the demarc; BFD 100/300, with stress tests that simulate route flap.

Action items / next steps:
- Naomi: please circulate the draft runbook checklist (I will merge infra items).
- Alex / Brightline: please confirm SIEM ingest formats and whether object storage snapshot access is acceptable for the optional KV snapshot flow.
- Schedule: Naomi's proposed Tue 2027-08-31 10:00 PT looks good for us. Please send a calendar invite; I will add a short 'failure modes' section to the agenda.

Attachments: runbook-checklist.md (draft) — I'll drop a more fleshed version into the shared drive after this thread.
